newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilean police re-enter German enclave.
newsitem.headline: Chilean police re-enter German enclave.

text.p: The Chilean police entered a secretive German settlement in the south of Chile for the second successive day on Wednesday, searching for fugitive enclave founder Paul Schaeffer.
Some 20 agents arrived in four vehicles on Wednesday morning in Villa Baviera, formerly known as Colonia Dignidad, to continue inspections they started on Tuesday.
Schaeffer, in his 80s, has had an arrest-warrant against him since November on charges of child abuse.
The latest search of the German compound, some 200 miles (320 kilometres) south of Santiago, surprised the settlers on Wednesday, a holiday in Chile.

Police Major Enrique Ramirez told reporters his mission was to continue inspections started the day before under orders from judge Hernan Gonzalez, appointed to investigate charges of child abuse made by several children who attended school at Villa Baviera.

"Our mission is to arrest Mr. Schaeffer," the head of Chile's police, Fernando Cordero, told reporters in the port of Valparaiso, northwest of Santiago, where he was attending festivities for the Naval Glories Day.
He said police hoped to detain Schaeffer, although members of the German community in the colony have denied he is there.
"I hope they find him", German ambassador to Chile Werner Reichenbaum told reporters after Tuesday's operation.
He said it was unacceptable that someone refused to appear before a court of justice when he faces such grave charges.
On Tuesday, a convoy of police vans and trucks passed the first gate of Colonia Dignidad (Dignity Colony) but stopped short of an inner gate leading into the shadowy community's living areas.

Two of Schaeffer's confidants, both German citizens, and two Chilean members of the settlement surrendered to police last week to face charges including the illegal detention of a child, obstruction of justice and the destruction of public property. All four were later released on bail.

Schaeffer set up the colony in the mid-1950s. It was protected by the former military regime of Gen. Augusto Pinochet, and human rights groups charged that the military used it as a secret detention and torture centre.

A special prosecutor appointed by President Eduardo Frei's government issued an arrest warrant for Schaeffer in 1996 on charges that he molested at least five Chilean boys who had been sent to a boarding school in the community.
The child abuse charges alienated the settlement'ss one-time allies among conservative Chilean politicians and the Roman Catholic Church, who have urged Schaeffer to give himself up.
